mainTopic: A widow who claims she was never given her מזונות (support) from her late husband's estate: who must bring proof, the widow or the יתומים?
overview: This amud continues רבי יוחנן's question about a widow who says the heirs never gave her מזונות (support). Whose possession is the estate in? If it is the יתומים', the widow must bring proof. If it is the widow's, the יתומים must bring proof. The גמרא first brings a ברייתא taught by לוי. It says that before she remarries the יתומים must bring proof, and after she remarries she must. Then רב שימי בר אשי says the question matches a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says a widow selling estate property must write whether each sale was for מזונות or for her כתובה. רבי יוסי says she may write a plain sale. The גמרא rejects this link in two ways. רבי יהודה may only be giving good advice, as a משנה does, so that no one calls her a glutton. Or רבי יוסי may only be giving her freedom to choose later, like the creditor in אביי קשישא's parable of the dying man who said 'give 200 זוז to my creditor.'

steps.title: Whose possession is the property in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the two sides of רבי יוחנן's question: is the estate in the יתומים' possession, so the widow needs proof, or in the widow's possession, so the יתומים need proof?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say the property is in the possession of the orphans, so the widow must bring proof? Or perhaps the property is in the possession of the widow, so the orphans must bring proof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible answers to the question of who must bring proof when a widow says she never got her מזונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that whoever wants to take something away from the one holding it must bring proof. So everything depends on who counts as 'holding' the property. Is it the יתומים, who inherited it, or the widow, whose כתובה gives her a claim on it?

keyTerms.meaning: property, assets (here, the estate of the husband who died)
in the established possession or status of
orphans, here meaning the husband's heirs
widow
to bring proof

phrases.english: Does the property stand in the possession of the orphans
and it is upon the widow to bring proof,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא נִכְסֵי בְּחֶזְקַת אַלְמָנָה קָיְימִי,
phrases.english: or perhaps the property stands in the possession of the widow,
and it is upon the orphans to bring proof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question רבי יוחנן started on the earlier part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the estate counts as being in the יתומים' possession or the widow's possession, which decides who carries the burden of proof about past מזונות.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא: it depends on whether she remarried
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught by לוי says that while the widow has not remarried, the יתומים must bring proof. Once she remarries, she must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what לוי taught: a widow, as long as she has not remarried, the orphans must bring proof. Once she has remarried, she must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question, and the answer is a split depending on whether the widow has remarried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not pick one side for every case. Before she remarries, the burden is on the יתומים. After she remarries and comes to claim past support, the burden switches to her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'come and hear', the גמרא's way of bringing a source to answer a question
taught (a ברייתא)
she got married (here, remarried)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the answer is one-sided. The ברייתא gives each side the burden at a different stage: the יתומים before remarriage, the widow after.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Levi taught:
A widow, as long as she has not remarried —
it is upon the orphans to bring proof
Once she has remarried — it is upon her to bring proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question raised in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Who carries the burden of proof about the widow's past מזונות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by לוי: before remarriage the יתומים must prove, after remarriage the widow must prove.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says the question matches a dispute between תנאים. רבי יהודה says a widow selling estate property must write which sales were for מזונות and which were for her כתובה. רבי יוסי says she may write it without saying, and this makes her position stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: it is like a dispute of תנאים. She sells and writes: 'These I sold for support' and 'These I sold for the כתובה.' These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: she sells and writes without saying what it was for, and this way her power is better.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי links our question to an older dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. He is setting up the next step, which shows how the two sides match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a widow selling parts of the estate. רבי יהודה requires her to label each sale: this for מזונות, this for the כתובה. רבי יוסי lets her write a plain sale with no label, which leaves her free to decide later how to count it, and that gives her a stronger position.

keyTerms.meaning: 'like the תנאים', meaning this matches a dispute between them
she sells (property from the estate)
support or maintenance owed to the widow
without saying what it is for
her position is stronger

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, כְּתַנָּאֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
She sells, and writes:
phrases.notes: 'She' is the widow, selling pieces of her late husband's property.

phrases.english: 'These I sold for support'
and 'These I sold for the ketubah,'
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מוֹכֶרֶת וְכוֹתֶבֶת סְתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: She sells and writes without specifying,
and in this way her power is better.
phrases.notes: With no label, she can decide later whether a sale counts toward support or toward the כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from solving the question with לוי's ברייתא to showing that the question itself is an old dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the widow must label each sale as being for מזונות or for her כתובה. רבי יוסי: she may write a plain sale, which strengthens her position.

steps.title: Matching each תנא to one side of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה requires labeling because he holds the property is in the יתומים' possession, so the widow must prove. רבי יוסי does not require it because he holds the property is in the widow's possession, so the יתומים must prove.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about exactly this? רבי יהודה, who says she must specify, holds: the property stands in the possession of the orphans, and the widow must bring proof. רבי יוסי holds she does not need to specify: the property stands in the possession of the widow, and the orphans must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי are arguing about the very question from step 1. Each one takes one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the widow has to prove her claims, she needs clear written records, so רבי יהודה makes her label each sale. If the יתומים carry the burden, she needs no labels, so רבי יוסי lets her write a plain sale. The phrase מאי לאו shows this is only a suggested reading, not yet a final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'is it not that...?', a way of proposing an explanation
they disagree
she needs to specify
he holds

steps.confusionAlert: This is a suggested way to explain the dispute (מאי לאו), not a final conclusion. Don't treat it as settled.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the question from the start: whose possession the property is in.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehuda, who said she must specify,
holds: the property stands in the possession of the orphans,
and it is upon the widow to bring proof.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: לָא בָּעֵי לְפָרוֹשֵׁי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds: she does not need to specify,
because the property stands in the possession of the widow,
and it is upon the orphans to bring proof.

steps.whatToRemember: רב שימי בר אשי's suggested reading: רבי יהודה (label each sale) means the property is in the יתומים' possession and the widow must prove. רבי יוסי (no label needed) means the property is in the widow's possession and the יתומים must prove.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a practical rule, how a widow writes up her sales, to the basic question of who carries the burden of proof in disputes over מזונות.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the dispute brought in step 3 matches the two sides of the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whose possession the property is in was already argued by תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about whether the widow must label her sales.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה is only giving good advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link from Step 4. Perhaps everyone agrees the property is in the widow's possession, and רבי יהודה's requirement to label the sales is only practical advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe everyone agrees that the property is in the widow's possession, so the יתומים must bring proof. רבי יהודה is just giving good advice, so that people will not call her a glutton.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about who holds the property. It suggests they might actually agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said רבי יהודה requires labeling because the widow carries the burden of proof. Here the גמרא says no: even if the יתומים carry the burden, labeling is wise. It protects her from the יתומים complaining that she spent too much on her food, so it is advice and not a legal rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? A challenge to an assumption.
Everyone, meaning both sides of the dispute agree
Good advice, a practical suggestion and not a binding law
Gluttony, being an overeater

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's rule is being reread here, not dropped. The גמרא does not say labeling is wrong. It says labeling may be smart advice and not proof of who holds the property.

phrases.english: From where do you know this? Perhaps everyone agrees
that the property stands in the widow's possession,
and the orphans must bring proof,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן —
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda is teaching us good advice:
so that they will not call her a glutton.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 4 that the תנאים argue about who holds the property.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of רבי יהודה as holding the property is in the יתומים' possession.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The labeling requirement can be explained as practical advice, so it does not prove who has the burden of proof.

steps.title: Proof that labeling can be just advice: the משנה about selling for food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the 'good advice' reading. A משנה also tells the widow to write 'these I sold for food.' If such wording proved who holds the property, רבי יוחנן would have solved his question from that משנה. So it must be advice, and the same applies to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not say this, then רבי יוחנן's question could have been answered from the משנה: she sells for food outside of court and writes, 'These I sold for food.' Rather, we cannot learn anything from the משנה, because it is only teaching good advice. Here too, רבי יהודה is teaching good advice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for what it just said in Step 5, using a משנה that has the same labeling instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If labeling meant that the property is in the יתומים' possession, the משנה would already answer רבי יוחנן's question, and רבי יוחנן would not have asked it. Since he did ask, the משנה's labeling must be only advice. That shows labeling instructions can be advice, so רבי יהודה's can be too.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you do not say so, an introduction to a proof by showing the other option fails
Resolve, answer an open question
Our משנה
Food and living support that the widow gets from the estate

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא method: if a source could have answered a great אמורא's question but he still asked it, then that source must not mean what we thought.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then the question that Rabbi Yoḥanan asked,
resolve it from the Mishna:
She sells for food not in court,
and writes: 'These I sold for food'!
Rather, nothing can be learned from the Mishna,
because it is teaching us good advice.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
phrases.english: Here too, he is teaching us good advice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'good advice' rejection in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That a labeling instruction can be good advice and not a sign of who holds the property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 97b, which tells the widow to write 'these I sold for food,' and the fact that רבי יוחנן still asked his question.

steps.title: Or maybe everyone holds the property is in the יתומים' possession
steps.stepSummary: A second way to reject the link: everyone may agree the property is in the יתומים' possession, and רבי יוסי's view is explained by a different reason, from אביי קשישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: everyone agrees the property is in the יתומים' possession, and this is the reason of רבי יוסי, as אביי קשישא explained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite way to say the תנאים do not argue about who holds the property. This line sets up אביי קשישא's parable in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 explained רבי יהודה without the possession question. This step does the same for רבי יוסי from the other side. Even if the widow carries the burden, רבי יוסי has another reason to let her leave the sales unlabeled.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively, or else
And this is the reason
אביי the Elder, an earlier sage with the same name

phrases.english: Alternatively: everyone agrees
that the property stands in the orphans' possession,
and this is the reason of Rabbi Yosei:
as Abaye the Elder explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second rejection of Step 4, the opposite of Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of רבי יוסי as holding the property is in the widow's possession.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's view can be explained by a different reason, so it does not prove who has the burden of proof.

steps.title: אביי קשישא's parable of the dying man and his creditor
steps.stepSummary: אביי קשישא compares רבי יוסי's view to a dying man who says 'give 200 זוז to so-and-so, my creditor.' The creditor may choose to take it as payment of his debt or as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי קשישא said: To what can רבי יוסי's view be compared? To a dying man who said, 'Give two hundred זוז to so-and-so, my creditor.' If the creditor wants, he takes it as payment of his debt. If he wants, he takes it as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי קשישא gives a parable to explain why רבי יוסי says leaving the sales unlabeled makes the widow's position stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dying man's unclear wording leaves the creditor free to choose whichever way helps him more. In the same way, when the widow does not label her sales, she keeps the choice to treat each sale as food or as כתובה, whichever suits her later. That flexibility is her advantage, even if the property is in the יתומים' possession.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a comparison
A dying person, whose spoken instructions about his property take effect
A creditor, someone who is owed money
A gift

steps.whatToRemember: The link between רבי יוחנן's question and the תנאים is rejected both ways. רבי יהודה may be giving only advice, or רבי יוסי may be giving the widow freedom of choice, like the creditor in אביי קשישא's parable.

phrases.english: For Abaye the Elder said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה?
phrases.english: A parable for Rabbi Yosei's view: what is it like?
It is like a dying man who said:
'Give two hundred zuz to so-and-so, my creditor,'
phrases.notes: 'Give' usually sounds like a gift. That is why the creditor gets to choose.

phrases.english: if he wants, he takes them as payment of his debt,
if he wants, he takes them as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the explanation of רבי יוסי that Step 7 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unclear wording that allows two ways of taking money gives the receiver the right to choose the better one. So the widow's unlabeled sales give her the same freedom.
